Step–1.  Protection  
(S)-4-Hydroxy­cyclohex-2-en-1-one → 4-O-TBS-cyclohex-2-en-1-one (compound 1).

Step–2.  Cuprate conjugate addition / enolate trapping  
Ph₂CuLi adds 1,4- to the enone.  
• The bulky TBSO group at C-4 occupies the favoured equatorial “up” position in the chair.  
• The cuprate therefore approaches from the opposite (down) face giving a β-phenyl group trans to OTBS at C-3.  
The conjugate addition generates the enolate at C-2 (α to the carbonyl) which is trapped by benzyl bromide.  
• Alkylation occurs from the less-hindered down face, giving the benzyl substituent trans to the OTBS and cis to the newly introduced phenyl.  
Product 2: trans-3-phenyl,2-benzyl-4-OTBS-cyclohexanone (C-2 and C-3 stereocentres set).

Step–3.  Regio- and diastereoselective α-methylation  
LDA at –78 °C removes the most accessible α-proton – the one at C-6 (the side opposite the bulky benzyl and phenyl groups), furnishing the kinetic enolate.  
Methyl iodide alkylates this enolate from the less-hindered down face, giving a methyl group trans to the OTBS (and therefore the 6S configuration).

Product 3 now possesses four stereocentres:  
C-2 S, C-3 R, C-4 S (original), C-6 S.

Step–4.  Deprotection  
Aqueous HCl removes the TBS group, regenerating the 4-hydroxy group and giving the final product 4.

Final structure: (2S,3R,4S,6S)-2-benzyl-4-hydroxy-6-methyl-3-phenyl­cyclohexan-1-one.

This corresponds to option (C).

Answer: C
